text:
The line regulation failure (0.567 V/V against a 0.029 limit) is the largest violation, and it points to the PMOS mirror rather than the bias core. M3, M4, and M5 should share the common mirror gate `g`, but M4's gate is tied to `vref`. That breaks the mirror's matching and couples the supply into the bias loop. The power overshoot (9.68 µW vs. 7.6 µW) is smaller and could also come from the mirror imbalance, or from R1 being undersized, so I rank the mirror devices above R1.

```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "M5", "R1"], "fault": "M4 gate is connected to vref instead of the common PMOS mirror gate g (should be M4 a g vdd vdd pfet), which unbalances the PMOS current mirror, degrades supply rejection (line regulation ~20x over spec), and contributes to the excess current/power."}
```
